doc: The same fields with a Hadley edge of 12 degrees (a fast rotator): x = |lat| / 12 reaches 7.5, the deck window (0.3 .. 1.25) covers a narrow band, and everything poleward is past it. Tolerance as surface_regime_weights.earth.hadley30. Arguments: the weights (w_closed, w_open, w_street = the dict entries closed, open, street), continentality and deck_strength (the two SurfaceTerms fields the function reads; the others are not read) and lat_rows (the latitude of each row in rad, broadcast over the columns as generate() does); hadley_deg is in params. Outputs closed, open, street (float32). Dtype chain to reproduce: sea = 1 - continentality and closed = w_closed sea are float32; deck = deck_window(x) deck_strength is float64 (x from the float64 latitudes); in closed + (1 - closed) deck the factor (1 - closed) is rounded to float32 BEFORE it meets the float64 deck, so closed (float64 from there on) can land a few 1e-8 above 1 and the scale (1 - closed) / rest then comes out slightly NEGATIVE (down to about -2.3e-8 on the open and street shares); the source does not clamp it and the stored outputs keep it. A float64 end-to-end port, or one that clamps the scale at 0, differs from this by at most that much (2.3e-8 on the stored cases), inside the tolerance: the negative shares are an artifact of that float32 rounding, not a contract. Measured: promoting the float32 inputs to float64 changes the output by at most 6.0e-8; one-ulp nudges of every float input and parameter change it by at most 1.4e-7 (worst of 6 random trials); the tolerance is 14x the larger of the two spreads.
